paper.title_en: Thermodynamic topological classification of magnetically charged slowly rotating Kerr black holes in nonlinear electrodynamics with a cosmological constant
paper.abstract_en: We provide an explicit rotating black-hole realization of the predicted \(\overline{W}^{1-}\) thermodynamic topological subclass by studying a slowly rotating, magnetically charged Kerr black hole in nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED). Using a reduced fixed-parameter off-shell potential, we derive the inverse-temperature curve analytically rather than relying solely on numerical plots. In AdS spacetime, this curve begins at a finite nonzero value, increases monotonically, and diverges at large horizon radius; it therefore contains exactly one defect with \(w=W=-1\) and has no stable large-black-hole branch. Positivity of the analytic coefficient establishes this result throughout the admissible slow-rotation parameter domain. Under the same reduced prescription, the Kerr-AdS benchmark instead has two branches and belongs to the \(W^{0-}\) class, establishing a clear topological distinction between the NLED-Kerr and classical rotating cases. In dS spacetime, the formally extended off-shell curve remains monotonic and any isolated zero has \(w=-1\); because the parameter-dependent horizon-admissible range is not fixed in the present reduced analysis, no physical dS asymptotic subclass is assigned.
